points: Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the tangent of the $x$–$t$ graph; instantaneous acceleration is the…
Displacement is the area under the $v$–$t$ graph; change in velocity is the area under the $a$–$t$ graph.
$v = 0$ does not imply $a = 0$ — turning points have zero velocity but non-zero acceleration.
Speeding up ⟺ $v$ and $a$ share the same sign; slowing down ⟺ opposite signs.
Derivatives go down the chain $x \to v \to a$; integrals go up $a \to v \to x$, using initial conditions.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Instantaneous velocity: $v = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0}\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = \frac{dx}{dt}$
Instantaneous acceleration: $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d^2x}{dt^2}$
Displacement from velocity: $x_2 - x_1 = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} v\,dt$ (area under $v$–$t$ curve)
Velocity from acceleration: $v_2 - v_1 = \int_{t_1}^{t_2} a\,dt$
Rest condition: $v = \frac{dx}{dt} = 0$; reversal check: sign change of $v$ around that instant

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Slope of $v$–$t$ = acceleration; area under $v$–$t$ = displacement.
The three equations hold ONLY for constant acceleration.
$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ is the equation of choice when time is unknown.
$s = \left(\frac{u+v}{2}\right)t$ is the graphical 'average velocity × time' form.
Sign convention decides deceleration: keep one positive direction throughout the problem.

branches.topic: Motion of a Freely Falling Body

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Free fall acceleration $g$ is independent of mass, size and material.
At every instant of the flight, $a = g$ downward — including the top ($v = 0$, $a \ne 0$).
Up–down symmetry: equal speeds at equal heights, equal times up and down.
Use ONE sign convention throughout a problem; put $g$'s sign in consistently.
'Dropped' = $u = 0$; 'thrown' = $u \ne 0$ — the equations differ by the $ut$ term.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Dropped from rest: $v = gt$, $h = \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2$, $v = \sqrt{2gh}$
Thrown up (up positive): $v = u - gt$, $h = ut - \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2$, $v^2 = u^2 - 2gh$
Maximum height: $h_{max} = \dfrac{u^2}{2g}$ (at $v = 0$)
Times: $t_{up} = t_{down} = \dfrac{u}{g}$, total flight $T = \dfrac{2u}{g}$
$n$-th second fall distance: $s_n = \tfrac{g}{2}(2n - 1)$ — ratio $1:3:5:7\ldots$

subtopics.name: Key points
points: Horizontal and vertical motions are independent; they share only TIME.
$v_x$ is constant; $v_y$ changes by $g$ every second; the path is a parabola.
At the top: $v_y = 0$, speed $= u\cos\theta$ (minimum), $a = g$ downward.
Landing speed equals launch speed; landing angle equals −launch angle (symmetry).
$R$ is maximum at 45°; complementary angles give equal ranges but different heights.

subtopics.name: Formulas & relations
points: Components: $v_x = u\cos\theta$ (constant); $v_y = u\sin\theta - gt$
Time of flight: $T = \dfrac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$
Maximum height: $H = \dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$
Range: $R = \dfrac{u^2\sin 2\theta}{g}$; $R_{max} = \dfrac{u^2}{g}$ at $\theta = 45°$
Trajectory: $y = x\tan\theta - \dfrac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$ (parabola); $R = 4H\cot\theta$
